footnote1: Footnote 1. Archetype picks the contact-quality rate shown for that hitter. Damage rate is the share of tracked fair batted balls with exit velocity of at least 95 mph and launch angle of at least 10 degrees. Tracked fair batted balls are Statcast pitches with type X and non-null exit velocity and launch angle. Barrel rate is Statcast barrel% (launch_speed_angle = 6) on that same denominator. The groups use 2026 regular-season competitive contact, which is those batted balls excluding bunts. A hitter is Damage when average exit velocity is at least 1.0 mph above the pooled MLB average of 88.0 mph. That is the power and high-exit-velocity group, graded on damage rate. A hitter is Barrel when average exit velocity is below that line. That is the average-exit-velocity group, graded on barrel rate. The two groups do not have to be the same size. Hitters with fewer than 30 competitive batted balls stay unclassified. The contact cell still shows the barrel or damage rate the exit-velocity rule would use, in italic gray, because the sample is too small. The superscript 1 marks Brooks Lee, Luke Keaschall, and Byron Buxton. Brooks Lee is the damage example. Luke Keaschall is the barrel example. Byron Buxton is Damage because he is a power and high-exit-velocity hitter. 2026 MLB average EV on competitive contact was 88.0 mph (n=124,098). 2026 MLB barrel rate was 7.7% (n=124,098 tracked batted balls, bunts included in that denominator). Brooks Lee’s 2026 competitive-contact average EV was 87.8 mph (n=488) and his barrel rate was 4.5%. Avg EV 87.8 mph is near the league average 88.0. Damage because he is a power hitter, the damage example. Final label: Damage. Luke Keaschall’s 2026 competitive-contact average EV was 84.8 mph (n=450) and his barrel rate was 3.8%. Avg EV 84.8 mph is below the league average 88.0. Barrel because he is an average-EV hitter, the barrel example. Final label: Barrel. Byron Buxton’s 2026 competitive-contact average EV was 90.2 mph (n=272) and his barrel rate was 15.8%. Avg EV 90.2 mph is +2.2 versus the league average 88.0. Damage because he is a power / high-EV hitter. Final label: Damage.
footnote2: Overall Execution is an equal-weight average of RISP knock-in, move-over, and QAB. Composite = (RISP knock-in + move-over + QAB) / 3, compared with the same average of the three league rates. Higher is better. White is within 1.5 percentage points of that league composite. If one input is missing, the cell averages the rates that exist. If none exist, the cell is blank. RISP knock-in is the share of plate appearances that begin with a runner on second and/or third in which the batter is credited with at least one RBI (MLB Stats API result.rbi on that plate appearance). Move-over denominator: plate appearances that begin with a runner on second, nobody on third, and 0 outs. A runner on first is allowed. Base-out state is the first tracked pitch of the plate appearance. Success: the runner who began the plate appearance on second has an end-of-PA state of safe at third (API movement end 3B) or safe at home (end score). He is not successful if he is out, if he never leaves second, or if he only touches third and is then retired. Advancement on the batted ball, a walk, hit-by-pitch, wild pitch, passed ball, balk, or stolen base during the plate appearance all count. A strikeout on which that runner does not end safe at third or home is a failure. QAB is the share of plate appearances with more than 5 pitches (6 or more Statcast pitches). Each month is compared with that month’s MLB rates. Last-10 rows use full-season 2026 MLB rates, because those games are not one shared month. 2026 MLB RISP knock-in rate was 24.2% (n=43,715 PA). 2026 MLB 0-out, second-to-third move-over rate was 56.2% (n=5,629 PA). 2026 MLB QAB rate (more than 5 pitches) was 20.6% (n=183,849 PA). September 2026 MLB RISP knock-in rate was 25.0% (n=6,463). September move-over rate was 55.8% (n=847). September QAB rate was 21.0% (n=27,294). League rates for the other columns: 2026 barrel% 7.7%, damage rate 22.2%, in-zone whiff 13.9%, chase 30.3%. September barrel% 7.7%, damage rate 22.1%, in-zone whiff 14.2%, chase 30.4%.

color_note: White band is within 10% of the comparison league rate, inclusive (ratio 0.90 to 1.10). Overall Execution is white within 1.5 percentage points of the league composite. Overall Execution averages the RISP, move-over, and QAB rates that exist. Italic gray = sample size too small. Small sample: under 8 tracked batted balls for contact quality, and also contact rates for hitters with fewer than 30 competitive batted balls. Those contact numbers are shown and are not colored green, red, or white. Under 10 in-zone swings, out-of-zone pitches, or plate-appearance opportunities for the other columns. Santurce hitter cards color a continuous blue-to-red magnitude scale (rateHeatStyle in pregame.html). This sheet uses the requested direction instead: white at the league band, green when the rate is better, red when it is worse. Header navy #122C6F matches the Santurce licey navy. Cell green and red are light fills so the numbers stay readable; they are not the Santurce magnitude gradient.
blank_note: Cells are blank when the denominator is zero. Overall Execution is blank only when RISP knock-in, move-over, and QAB are all missing. A hitter with no plate appearances in the selected month is left off that month, with no zero rates. When a hitter has fewer than 30 competitive batted balls, the archetype stays unclassified and the contact cell shows the barrel or damage rate in italic gray. That cell stays blank only when the window has no tracked batted balls. No rate was imputed from a nearby player, from a career norm, or from memory.
